title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: Grothendieck's 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. For each N there is a complex A_N^• of differential forms on the standard N-simplex: polynomial forms with divided powers, so that the Poincaré lemma holds over Z. It has de Rham differential d: A_N^i → A_N^{i+1} and a 'boundary' ∂: A_N^i → A_{N-1}^i, the alternating sum of restrictions to the faces. One has d∂ = ∂d, so (A_N^i, d, ∂) is a bicomplex (the cosimplicial PD de Rham algebra, read through its Moore complex). It is augmented by the constants ε_N: A_0 → A_N^0. The augmentation row is 0 ← A_0 ←0 A_0 ←id A_0 ←0 ..., the Moore complex of the constant simplicial object. The goal is to define integration maps K_N: A_N^N → A_0 inductively by 'Stokes'. Every top form is exact, ω^N = dω^{N-1}, because H^N(A_N^•)=0 for N≥1. One then sets K_N(ω^N) := K_{N-1}(∂ω^{N-1}). The page proves this is well defined, i.e. dω^{N-1}=0 implies K_{N-1}(∂ω^{N-1})=0. (a) If N≥2, H^{N-1}(A_N^•)=0 gives ω^{N-1}=dα^{N-2}. Then ∂ω^{N-1} = d∂α^{N-2}, and Stokes at the previous level turns this into ∂∂α^{N-2}=0. (b) If N=1, a closed 0-form is a constant ε_1(α), and ∂ε_1(α)=0 (the face difference of a constant). Remark 1 isolates exactly what was used: the degree conditions plus H^N(A_N)=0 (N≥1), H^{N-1}(A_N)=0 (N≥2) and H^0(A_1)=ε_1(A_0). Remark 2 says the whole argument works for an abstract augmented bicomplex in any abelian category satisfying: A_N^i=0 for i∉[0,N], d∂=∂d, and these cohomological conditions. The marginal note seems to say one may even take (Ab)^op. Remark 3 draws a consequence: uniqueness plus the abelian-category version imply the integrations A_n^n → A_0 commute with all endomorphisms of the system. Hence they are automatically linear for any module structure. In short, this is an axiomatic, Stokes-determined characterization of integration over simplices, used to build an integral (PD) de Rham theorem.
errors: Index slip: the 'Stokes' step should read K_{N-1}(d∂α^{N-2}) = K_{N-2}(∂∂α^{N-2}) by the inductive definition, not K_{N-1}(∂∂α). This is harmless.
In the abstract conditions, 'H^0(A_1)=Ker δ' should be read as 'equals the image of ε_1', presumably ker of the relevant ∂/augmentation map. The notation δ is undefined on the page.
Remark 3 ('unicité') is asserted rather than proved. Uniqueness needs normalization of K_0 = id and the Stokes recursion; implicit but fine.

ideas.what: Integration over simplices of polynomial (divided-power) forms defined purely by Stokes' formula and the acyclicity of the simplex de Rham complexes, with a well-definedness check
ideas.modern_name: Integration map from simplicial polynomial de Rham forms to cochains (de Rham theorem for Sullivan/PL forms), integral PD version
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) and Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976) rationally; integral/divided-power versions by Cenkl–Porter and later authors
ideas.where_published: Only the unpublished 1976 IHES lecture; unsure of any circulated notes

ideas.what: Abstract version: augmented bicomplex in an arbitrary abelian category with degree and cohomology-vanishing conditions yields canonical 'integration' maps A_n^n → A_0
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic characterization of integration / Stokes maps for acyclic cosimplicial de Rham objects (uniqueness of the de Rham comparison)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; closest are acyclic-models style uniqueness arguments

ideas.what: Naturality: integration commutes with all endomorphisms, hence respects module structures, deduced from uniqueness in the abelian-category formulation

missed.claim: Grothendieck gives an axiomatic, coefficient-free (any abelian category) characterization of integration over simplices for the divided-power de Rham complex. This underlies an integral de Rham comparison for simplicial sets via PD polynomial forms, which the literature developed independently later (Cenkl–Porter and others).
missed.quote: On peut donner une version "abstrait" en termes d'un bicomplexe augmenté avec des conditions de degrés qu'il faut (et dd∂=∂d) dans une cat. abélienne
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic models of homotopy types via divided-power or cosimplicial de Rham algebras are active again. This documents Grothendieck's 1976 priority on the PD simplicial de Rham idea, though the argument on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine Stokes/well-definedness verification. Mildly interesting as historical evidence that Grothendieck in 1976 axiomatized integration for PD simplicial de Rham complexes, but the mathematics is standard.
transcription_corrections: Previous and next page transcriptions belong to a different document (SGA 7 IX, Néron models), not this manuscript.
Marginal note in Remark 2 likely reads '[il faut pour être (Ab)° !]' or similar, i.e. the abstract setting allows the opposite category of abelian groups; reading uncertain.
'Dans {+la ligne+} (1)' is better read 'Dans (1)', with an inserted word above, probably 'la preuve de'.

Remark 3 likely begins 'À cause de l'unicité, grâce à la version "cat. abélienne", on voit que les "intégrations" A_n^n → A_0^0 = A_0 commutent à tous les endos des A_α^α – donc respectent une éventuelle structure de module'.
